1	"""Lexer, parser and semantic validation for the OpenQASM 2.0 subset.
2	
3	Supported subset::
4	
5	    OPENQASM 2.0;
6	    include "qelib1.inc";
7	    qreg name[positive-size];
8	    creg name[positive-size];
9	    x qubit;
10	    h qubit;
11	    cx qubit, qubit;
12	    cz qubit, qubit;
13	    rx(angle) qubit;
14	    ry(angle) qubit;
15	    rz(angle) qubit;
16	    crx(angle) qubit, qubit;
17	    cry(angle) qubit, qubit;
18	    crz(angle) qubit, qubit;
19	    measure qubit -> cbit;
20	
21	Only one ``qreg`` and one ``creg`` may be declared, and gates/measures only
22	accept single bits with constant integer indices. Line comments (``//``) are
23	supported.
24	
25	Angle expressions are written in radians and may use decimal integer and
26	real literals (including scientific notation), the constant ``pi``,
27	parentheses, unary ``+``/``-`` and the binary operators ``+``, ``-``, ``*``
28	and ``/`` with the usual precedence (``*``/``/`` before ``+``/``-``, same
29	precedence evaluated left to right, parentheses first).
30	"""
31	
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import math
35	from dataclasses import dataclass
36	
37	
38	class ParseError(Exception):
39	    """A lexical or syntactic problem (reported as ``parse_error``)."""
40	
41	    def __init__(self, message: str, line: int, column: int):
42	        super().__init__(message)
43	        self.message = message
44	        self.line = line
45	        self.column = column
46	
47	
48	class ValidationError(Exception):
49	    """A syntactically valid but semantically invalid program."""
50	
51	    def __init__(self, message: str, line: int, column: int):
52	        super().__init__(message)
53	        self.message = message
54	        self.line = line
55	        self.column = column
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True)
59	class Token:
60	    kind: str  # 'ident', 'int', 'real', 'string' or a literal punctuation word
61	    value: str
62	    line: int  # 1-based
63	    column: int  # 1-based, points at the first character of the token
64	
65	
66	_KEYWORDS = {"OPENQASM", "include", "qreg", "creg", "measure"}
67	_BUILTIN_GATES = {"x", "h", "cx", "cz", "rx", "ry", "rz", "crx", "cry", "crz"}
68	_PARAMETERIZED_GATES = {"rx", "ry", "rz"}
69	_CONTROLLED_GATES = {"cx", "cz"}
70	_CONTROLLED_PARAMETERIZED_GATES = {"crx", "cry", "crz"}
71	
72	# A state vector has 2**n amplitudes; larger registers cannot be simulated
73	# and are rejected as illegal sizes rather than crashing.
74	_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE = 20
75	
76	
77	def tokenize(source: str) -> list[Token]:
78	    """Split *source* into tokens.
79	
80	    Raises :class:`ParseError` (with 1-based position) on invalid input.
81	    """
82	    tokens: list[Token] = []
83	    line = 1
84	    col = 1
85	    n = len(source)
86	    i = 0
87	
88	    while i < n:
89	        ch = source[i]
90	
91	        if ch == "\n":
92	            i += 1
93	            line += 1
94	            col = 1
95	            continue
96	        if ch in " \t\r":
97	            i += 1
98	            col += 1
99	            continue
100	
101	        # Line comment: runs to end of line (end of input also terminates it).
102	        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < n and source[i + 1] == "/":
103	            i += 2
104	            col += 2
105	            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
106	                i += 1
107	                col += 1
108	            continue
109	
110	        start_line, start_col = line, col
111	
112	        if ch.isalpha() or ch == "_":
113	            j = i + 1
114	            while j < n and (source[j].isalnum() or source[j] == "_"):
115	                j += 1
116	            word = source[i:j]
117	            kind = word if word in _KEYWORDS else "ident"
118	            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
119	            col += j - i
120	            i = j
121	            continue
122	
123	        if ch.isdigit() or (ch == "." and i + 1 < n and source[i + 1].isdigit()):
124	            j = i
125	            seen_dot = False
126	            seen_exp = False
127	            while j < n:
128	                c = source[j]
129	                if c.isdigit():
130	                    j += 1
131	                elif c == "." and not seen_dot and not seen_exp:
132	                    seen_dot = True
133	                    j += 1
134	                elif c in "eE" and not seen_exp:
135	                    seen_exp = True
136	                    j += 1
137	                    if j < n and source[j] in "+-":
138	                        j += 1
139	                else:
140	                    break
141	            word = source[i:j]
142	            kind = "real" if seen_dot or seen_exp else "int"
143	            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
144	            col += j - i
145	            i = j
146	            continue
147	
148	        if ch == '"':
149	            j = i + 1
150	            while j < n and source[j] != '"':
151	                if source[j] == "\n":
152	                    raise ParseError("unterminated string literal", start_line, start_col)
153	                j += 1
154	            if j >= n:
155	                raise ParseError("unterminated string literal", start_line, start_col)
156	            tokens.append(Token("string", source[i + 1 : j], start_line, start_col))
157	            col += j - i + 1
158	            i = j + 1
159	            continue
160	
161	        if ch == "-" and i + 1 < n and source[i + 1] == ">":
162	            tokens.append(Token("->", "->", start_line, start_col))
163	            i += 2
164	            col += 2
165	            continue
166	
167	        if ch in "[];,()+*/-":
168	            tokens.append(Token(ch, ch, start_line, start_col))
169	            i += 1
170	            col += 1
171	            continue
172	
173	        raise ParseError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
174	
175	    tokens.append(Token("eof", "", line, col))
176	    return tokens
177	
178	
179	@dataclass(frozen=True)
180	class Operation:
181	    """A validated gate application or measurement."""
182	
183	    kind: str  # 'x', 'h', 'cx', 'cz', 'rx', 'ry', 'rz', 'crx', 'cry', 'crz' or 'measure'
184	    targets: tuple[int, ...]  # qubit indices; measure appends the cbit index
185	    params: tuple[float, ...] = ()  # gate angles in radians (rx/ry/rz/crx/cry/crz only)
186	
187	
188	@dataclass(frozen=True)
189	class Program:
190	    num_qubits: int
191	    num_clbits: int
192	    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]
193	
194	
195	def _parse_decimal(token: Token) -> int:
196	    """Parse a non-negative decimal literal, rejecting oversized ones."""
197	    if len(token.value) > 18:
198	        raise ValidationError("integer literal is too large", token.line, token.column)
199	    return int(token.value)
200	
201	
202	def parse(source: str) -> Program:
203	    """Parse and validate the OpenQASM subset, returning a :class:`Program`."""
204	    tokens = tokenize(source)
205	    pos = 0
206	
207	    def peek() -> Token:
208	        return tokens[pos]
209	
210	    def advance() -> Token:
211	        nonlocal pos
212	        tok = tokens[pos]
213	        pos += 1
214	        return tok
215	
216	    def expect(kind: str) -> Token:
217	        tok = peek()
218	        if tok.kind != kind:
219	            raise ParseError(f"expected {kind!r} but found {tok.value!r}", tok.line, tok.column)
220	        return advance()
221	
222	    # Header: OPENQASM 2.0;  (a real token "2.0", exactly)
223	    first = peek()
224	    if first.kind != "OPENQASM":
225	        raise ParseError("expected 'OPENQASM' declaration", first.line, first.column)
226	    advance()
227	    version = expect("real") if peek().kind == "real" else expect("int")
228	    if version.value != "2.0":
229	        raise ParseError(f"unsupported OpenQASM version {version.value!r}", version.line, version.column)
230	    expect(";")
231	
232	    # Exactly: include "qelib1.inc";
233	    expect("include")
234	    path = expect("string")
235	    if path.value != "qelib1.inc":
236	        raise ValidationError(f"unknown include file {path.value!r}", path.line, path.column)
237	    expect(";")
238	
239	    qreg_name: str | None = None
240	    qreg_size: int | None = None
241	    creg_name: str | None = None
242	    creg_size: int | None = None
243	    operations: list[Operation] = []
244	    measured_qubits: set[int] = set()
245	    measured_clbits: set[int] = set()
246	    measurement_started = False
247	
248	    def parse_index(reg_kind: str) -> tuple[int, Token, Token]:
249	        """Parse ``name[const]`` returning (index, name token, index token)."""
250	        name_tok = expect("ident")
251	        expect("[")
252	        idx_tok = expect("int")
253	        expect("]")
254	        if reg_kind == "q":
255	            if name_tok.value != qreg_name:
256	                if creg_name is not None and name_tok.value == creg_name:
257	                    raise ValidationError(
258	                        "classical register used where a quantum register is required",
259	                        name_tok.line,
260	                        name_tok.column,
261	                    )
262	                raise ValidationError(
263	                    f"undeclared quantum register {name_tok.value!r}",
264	                    name_tok.line,
265	                    name_tok.column,
266	                )
267	            size = qreg_size
268	        else:
269	            if name_tok.value != creg_name:
270	                if qreg_name is not None and name_tok.value == qreg_name:
271	                    raise ValidationError(
272	                        "quantum register used where a classical register is required",
273	                        name_tok.line,
274	                        name_tok.column,
275	                    )
276	                raise ValidationError(
277	                    f"undeclared classical register {name_tok.value!r}",
278	                    name_tok.line,
279	                    name_tok.column,
280	                )
281	            size = creg_size
282	        idx = _parse_decimal(idx_tok)
283	        assert size is not None
284	        if not 0 <= idx < size:
285	            raise ValidationError(
286	                f"register index {idx} out of range for register of size {size}",
287	                idx_tok.line,
288	                idx_tok.column,
289	            )
290	        return idx, name_tok, idx_tok
291	
292	    def parse_angle() -> float:
293	        """Parse and evaluate an angle expression (result in radians).
294	
295	        Grammar (usual precedence, left associativity, parentheses first)::
296	
297	            expr    := term (('+' | '-') term)*
298	            term    := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
299	            factor  := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
300	            atom    := int | real | 'pi' | '(' expr ')'
301	        """
302	
303	        def check_finite(value: float, op_tok: Token) -> float:
304	            if not math.isfinite(value):
305	                raise ValidationError(
306	                    "angle expression result is not a finite number",
307	                    op_tok.line,
308	                    op_tok.column,
309	                )
310	            return value
311	
312	        def parse_atom() -> float:
313	            tok = peek()
314	            if tok.kind == "int":
315	                advance()
316	                return float(_parse_decimal(tok))
317	            if tok.kind == "real":
318	                advance()
319	                try:
320	                    value = float(tok.value)
321	                except ValueError:
322	                    raise ParseError(
323	                        f"malformed numeric literal {tok.value!r}",
324	                        tok.line,
325	                        tok.column,
326	                    ) from None
327	                if not math.isfinite(value):
328	                    raise ValidationError(
329	                        f"numeric literal {tok.value!r} is too large",
330	                        tok.line,
331	                        tok.column,
332	                    )
333	                return value
334	            if tok.kind == "ident":
335	                advance()
336	                if tok.value == "pi":
337	                    return math.pi
338	                raise ValidationError(
339	                    f"unknown name {tok.value!r} in angle expression",
340	                    tok.line,
341	                    tok.column,
342	                )
343	            if tok.kind == "(":
344	                advance()
345	                value = parse_expr()
346	                expect(")")
347	                return value
348	            raise ParseError(
349	                f"expected a number, 'pi' or '(' but found {tok.value!r}",
350	                tok.line,
351	                tok.column,
352	            )
353	
354	        def parse_factor() -> float:
355	            tok = peek()
356	            if tok.kind == "+" or tok.kind == "-":
357	                advance()
358	                operand = parse_factor()
359	                return operand if tok.kind == "+" else -operand
360	            return parse_atom()
361	
362	        def parse_term() -> float:
363	            value = parse_factor()
364	            while peek().kind == "*" or peek().kind == "/":
365	                op_tok = advance()
366	                rhs = parse_factor()
367	                if op_tok.kind == "*":
368	                    value = check_finite(value * rhs, op_tok)
369	                else:
370	                    if rhs == 0.0:
371	                        raise ValidationError(
372	                            "division by zero in angle expression",
373	                            op_tok.line,
374	                            op_tok.column,
375	                        )
376	                    value = check_finite(value / rhs, op_tok)
377	            return value
378	
379	        def parse_expr() -> float:
380	            value = parse_term()
381	            while peek().kind == "+" or peek().kind == "-":
382	                op_tok = advance()
383	                rhs = parse_term()
384	                if op_tok.kind == "+":
385	                    value = check_finite(value + rhs, op_tok)
386	                else:
387	                    value = check_finite(value - rhs, op_tok)
388	            return value
389	
390	        return parse_expr()
391	
392	    while peek().kind != "eof":
393	        tok = peek()
394	
395	        if tok.kind == "qreg" or tok.kind == "creg":
396	            advance()
397	            is_qreg = tok.kind == "qreg"
398	            name_tok = expect("ident")
399	            expect("[")
400	            size_tok = expect("int")
401	            expect("]")
402	            expect(";")
403	            size = _parse_decimal(size_tok)
404	            if not 1 <= size <= _MAX_REGISTER_SIZE:
405	                raise ValidationError(
406	                    f"register size must be between 1 and {_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE}, got {size}",
407	                    size_tok.line,
408	                    size_tok.column,
409	                )
410	            if is_qreg:
411	                if qreg_name is not None:
412	                    raise ValidationError(
413	                        "duplicate declaration of quantum register",
414	                        name_tok.line,
415	                        name_tok.column,
416	                    )
417	                if creg_name is not None and name_tok.value == creg_name:
418	                    raise ValidationError(
419	                        f"register name {name_tok.value!r} already declared",
420	                        name_tok.line,
421	                        name_tok.column,
422	                    )
423	                qreg_name = name_tok.value
424	                qreg_size = size
425	            else:
426	                if creg_name is not None:
427	                    raise ValidationError(
428	                        "duplicate declaration of classical register",
429	                        name_tok.line,
430	                        name_tok.column,
431	                    )
432	                if qreg_name is not None and name_tok.value == qreg_name:
433	                    raise ValidationError(
434	                        f"register name {name_tok.value!r} already declared",
435	                        name_tok.line,
436	                        name_tok.column,
437	                    )
438	                creg_name = name_tok.value
439	                creg_size = size
440	            continue
441	
442	        if tok.kind == "measure":
443	            advance()
444	            q_idx, q_name_tok, _q_idx_tok = parse_index("q")
445	            expect("->")
446	            c_idx, c_name_tok, _c_idx_tok = parse_index("c")
447	            expect(";")
448	            if q_idx in measured_qubits:
449	                raise ValidationError(
450	                    f"qubit {qreg_name}[{q_idx}] is measured more than once",
451	                    q_name_tok.line,
452	                    q_name_tok.column,
453	                )
454	            if c_idx in measured_clbits:
455	                raise ValidationError(
456	                    f"clbit {creg_name}[{c_idx}] is the target of more than one measurement",
457	                    c_name_tok.line,
458	                    c_name_tok.column,
459	                )
460	            measured_qubits.add(q_idx)
461	            measured_clbits.add(c_idx)
462	            measurement_started = True
463	            operations.append(Operation("measure", (q_idx, c_idx)))
464	            continue
465	
466	        if tok.kind == "ident":
467	            gate_name = tok.value
468	            if gate_name not in _BUILTIN_GATES:
469	                raise ValidationError(
470	                    f"undeclared identifier or unsupported gate {gate_name!r}",
471	                    tok.line,
472	                    tok.column,
473	                )
474	            if measurement_started:
475	                raise ValidationError(
476	                    f"quantum gate {gate_name!r} appears after a measurement",
477	                    tok.line,
478	                    tok.column,
479	                )
480	            advance()
481	            if gate_name in _CONTROLLED_GATES:
482	                ctrl, _, _ = parse_index("q")
483	                expect(",")
484	                tgt, tgt_name_tok, _ = parse_index("q")
485	                expect(";")
486	                if ctrl == tgt:
487	                    raise ValidationError(
488	                        f"{gate_name} control and target must be different qubits",
489	                        tgt_name_tok.line,
490	                        tgt_name_tok.column,
491	                    )
492	                operations.append(Operation(gate_name, (ctrl, tgt)))
493	            elif gate_name in _CONTROLLED_PARAMETERIZED_GATES:
494	                expect("(")
495	                angle = parse_angle()
496	                if peek().kind == ",":
497	                    comma = peek()
498	                    raise ParseError(
499	                        f"gate {gate_name!r} takes exactly one angle parameter",
500	                        comma.line,
501	                        comma.column,
502	                    )
503	                expect(")")
504	                ctrl, _, _ = parse_index("q")
505	                expect(",")
506	                tgt, tgt_name_tok, _ = parse_index("q")
507	                expect(";")
508	                if ctrl == tgt:
509	                    raise ValidationError(
510	                        f"{gate_name} control and target must be different qubits",
511	                        tgt_name_tok.line,
512	                        tgt_name_tok.column,
513	                    )
514	                operations.append(Operation(gate_name, (ctrl, tgt), (angle,)))
515	            elif gate_name in _PARAMETERIZED_GATES:
516	                expect("(")
517	                angle = parse_angle()
518	                if peek().kind == ",":
519	                    comma = peek()
520	                    raise ParseError(
521	                        f"gate {gate_name!r} takes exactly one angle parameter",
522	                        comma.line,
523	                        comma.column,

"""Density-matrix simulation with configurable noise channels.

Enabled via ``simulate --noise-model PATH``. The model is a JSON object with
up to four channel keys (probabilities in ``[0, 1]``):

- ``amplitude_damping``: |1> decays to |0> with probability gamma.
- ``phase_damping``: populations unchanged, off-diagonal entries scaled by
  ``1 - gamma``.
- ``bit_flip``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p X rho X``.
- ``depolarizing``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p I/2`` (the qubit is replaced by
  the maximally mixed state with probability ``p``).

After every quantum gate, each configured channel is applied to every qubit
the gate touched. Qubits of a two-qubit gate (``cx``, ``cz``, ``crx``,
``cry``, ``crz``) are processed in ascending index order; channels on one
qubit are applied in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER` order.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import json
import math

from .openqasm import Program

# Fixed order in which channels are applied per qubit and echoed back.
CHANNEL_ORDER = ("amplitude_damping", "phase_damping", "bit_flip", "depolarizing")

# A density matrix holds 4**n entries, so noisy simulation is capped well
# below the state-vector register limit.
MAX_NOISE_QUBITS = 10

_SQRT1_2 = 2.0**-0.5


class NoiseModelError(Exception):
    """The noise model content is invalid (reported as ``noise_model_error``)."""


def _reject_constant(value: str) -> None:
    # json accepts NaN/Infinity by default; they are not valid JSON numbers.
    raise NoiseModelError(f"noise model contains non-JSON constant {value!r}")


def _object_pairs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
    result: dict[str, object] = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"duplicate key {key!r} in noise model")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def parse_noise_model(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Parse and validate noise-model JSON text.

    Returns the configured channels as a mapping in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER`
    order with float probabilities, so models differing only in whitespace
    or key order produce identical output. Raises :class:`NoiseModelError`
    on any invalid content.
    """
    try:
        data = json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=_object_pairs, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise NoiseModelError(f"noise model is not valid JSON: {exc}") from None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must be a JSON object")
    if not data:
        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must configure at least one channel")
    for key, value in data.items():
        if key not in CHANNEL_ORDER:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"unknown noise channel {key!r}")
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be a JSON number")
        probability = float(value)
        if not math.isfinite(probability):
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be finite")
        if not 0.0 <= probability <= 1.0:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be between 0 and 1")
    return {channel: float(data[channel]) for channel in CHANNEL_ORDER if channel in data}


def _basis_offsets(size: int, bit: int):
    """Yield indices below *size* whose ``bit`` is clear, block by block."""
    step = bit << 1
    for base in range(0, size, step):
        yield from range(base, base + bit)


def _gate_matrix(kind: str, params: tuple[float, ...]) -> tuple[complex, complex, complex, complex]:
    if kind == "x":
        return (0j, 1 + 0j, 1 + 0j, 0j)
    if kind == "h":
        return (_SQRT1_2, _SQRT1_2, _SQRT1_2, -_SQRT1_2)
    theta = params[0]
    c = math.cos(theta / 2)
    s = math.sin(theta / 2)
    if kind == "rx":
        return (c, -1j * s, -1j * s, c)
    if kind == "ry":
        return (c, -s, s, c)
    if kind == "rz":
        return (cmath.exp(-0.5j * theta), 0j, 0j, cmath.exp(0.5j * theta))
    raise AssertionError(f"no single-qubit matrix for gate {kind!r}")


def _apply_single_qubit(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, matrix) -> None:
    """Apply ``rho -> U rho U†`` for a single-qubit unitary ``U``."""
    bit = 1 << qubit
    g00, g01, g10, g11 = matrix
    h00, h01 = g00.conjugate(), g01.conjugate()
    h10, h11 = g10.conjugate(), g11.conjugate()
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m00 = row0[j0]
            m01 = row0[j1]
            m10 = row1[j0]
            m11 = row1[j1]
            t00 = g00 * m00 + g01 * m10
            t01 = g00 * m01 + g01 * m11
            t10 = g10 * m00 + g11 * m10
            t11 = g10 * m01 + g11 * m11
            row0[j0] = t00 * h00 + t01 * h01
            row0[j1] = t00 * h10 + t01 * h11
            row1[j0] = t10 * h00 + t11 * h01
            row1[j1] = t10 * h10 + t11 * h11


def _apply_cx(rho: list[list[complex]], control: int, target: int, size: int) -> None:
    """Apply the cx basis permutation to both axes of the density matrix."""
    cbit = 1 << control
    tbit = 1 << target
    swapped = [i for i in range(size) if (i & cbit) and not (i & tbit)]
    for i in swapped:
        j = i | tbit
        rho[i], rho[j] = rho[j], rho[i]
    for i in swapped:
        j = i | tbit
        for row in rho:
            row[i], row[j] = row[j], row[i]


def _apply_controlled(
    rho: list[list[complex]], control: int, target: int, size: int, matrix
) -> None:
    """Apply ``rho -> U rho U†`` for a controlled single-qubit unitary.

    ``U`` acts as the single-qubit *matrix* on *target* when the *control*
    bit is 1 and as the identity otherwise. Done as a left pass (rows whose
    control bit is set) followed by a right pass (columns whose control bit
    is set), which also covers the cross blocks between the two sectors.
    """
    cbit = 1 << control
    tbit = 1 << target
    g00, g01, g10, g11 = matrix
    h00, h01 = g00.conjugate(), g01.conjugate()
    h10, h11 = g10.conjugate(), g11.conjugate()
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, tbit):
        if not (i0 & cbit):
            continue
        i1 = i0 | tbit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j in range(size):
            m0 = row0[j]
            m1 = row1[j]
            row0[j] = g00 * m0 + g01 * m1
            row1[j] = g10 * m0 + g11 * m1
    for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, tbit):
        if not (j0 & cbit):
            continue
        j1 = j0 | tbit
        for i in range(size):
            row = rho[i]
            m0 = row[j0]
            m1 = row[j1]
            row[j0] = m0 * h00 + m1 * h01
            row[j1] = m0 * h10 + m1 * h11


def _amplitude_damping(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, gamma: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    scale = math.sqrt(1.0 - gamma)
    damped = 1.0 - gamma
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m11 = row1[j1]
            row0[j0] = row0[j0] + gamma * m11
            row0[j1] = scale * row0[j1]
            row1[j0] = scale * row1[j0]
            row1[j1] = damped * m11


def _phase_damping(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, gamma: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    factor = 1.0 - gamma
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            row0[j1] = factor * row0[j1]
            row1[j0] = factor * row1[j0]


def _bit_flip(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, p: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    keep = 1.0 - p
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m00 = row0[j0]
            m01 = row0[j1]
            m10 = row1[j0]
            m11 = row1[j1]
            row0[j0] = keep * m00 + p * m11
            row0[j1] = keep * m01 + p * m10
            row1[j0] = keep * m10 + p * m01
            row1[j1] = keep * m11 + p * m00


def _depolarizing(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, p: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    keep = 1.0 - p
    half = p * 0.5
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m00 = row0[j0]
            m11 = row1[j1]
            mixed = half * (m00 + m11)
            row0[j0] = keep * m00 + mixed
            row1[j1] = keep * m11 + mixed
            row0[j1] = keep * row0[j1]
            row1[j0] = keep * row1[j0]


_CHANNELS = {
    "amplitude_damping": _amplitude_damping,
    "phase_damping": _phase_damping,
    "bit_flip": _bit_flip,
    "depolarizing": _depolarizing,
}


def simulate_density_matrix(program: Program, noise: dict[str, float]) -> list[float]:
    """Evolve the density matrix under all gates and noise channels.

    Returns the diagonal of the final density matrix (measurement
    probabilities per basis state). Measurements do not collapse the state,
    matching the state-vector path. Noise evolution is deterministic and
    consumes no randomness.
    """
    n = program.num_qubits
    size = 1 << n
    rho = [[0j] * size for _ in range(size)]
    rho[0][0] = 1 + 0j

    for op in program.operations:
        if op.kind == "measure":
            continue
        if op.kind == "cx":
            _apply_cx(rho, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], size)
        elif op.kind == "cz":
            _apply_controlled(
                rho, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], size, (1 + 0j, 0j, 0j, -1 + 0j)
            )
        elif op.kind in ("crx", "cry", "crz"):
            matrix = _gate_matrix(op.kind[1:], op.params)
            _apply_controlled(rho, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], size, matrix)
        else:
            _apply_single_qubit(rho, op.targets[0], size, _gate_matrix(op.kind, op.params))
        for qubit in sorted(set(op.targets)):
            for channel in CHANNEL_ORDER:
                probability = noise.get(channel)
                if probability:
                    _CHANNELS[channel](rho, qubit, size, probability)

    return [rho[i][i].real for i in range(size)]

147	def _write_output_atomic(target: str, data: bytes) -> str | None:
148	    """Write *data* to *target* without ever leaving a partial result.
149	
150	    Returns ``None`` on success, otherwise a human-readable error message.
151	    The data lands in a temporary file in the target's parent directory and
152	    is moved into place atomically, so a failure leaves any pre-existing
153	    target byte-for-byte unchanged and removes the temporary file.
154	    """
155	    parent = os.path.dirname(target) or "."
156	    if not os.path.isdir(parent):
157	        return f"cannot write output {target!r}: parent directory does not exist"
158	
159	    # The target may be a new file or an existing regular file. Symlinks are
160	    # followed (a link to a regular file is a valid target; os.replace swaps
161	    # the link itself without touching its referent), while a directory --
162	    # including a symlink to one -- and other non-regular types are refused.
163	    try:
164	        existing = os.stat(target)
165	    except FileNotFoundError:
166	        existing = None
167	    except OSError as exc:
168	        return f"cannot write output {target!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}"
169	    if existing is not None and not stat.S_ISREG(existing.st_mode):
170	        kind = "a directory" if stat.S_ISDIR(existing.st_mode) else "not a regular file"
171	        return f"cannot write output {target!r}: target is {kind}"
172	
173	    tmp_name: str | None = None
174	    try:
175	        try:
176	            fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".qcs-output-", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent)
177	        except OSError as exc:
178	            return f"cannot write output {target!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}"
179	        try:
180	            # A new file gets the usual umask-derived mode; overwriting an
181	            # existing regular file keeps its permissions (as open("w") would).
182	            current_umask = os.umask(0)
183	            os.umask(current_umask)
184	            mode = (
185	                stat.S_IMODE(existing.st_mode)
186	                if existing is not None
187	                else 0o666 & ~current_umask
188	            )
189	            os.fchmod(fd, mode)
190	            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
191	                handle.write(data)
192	                handle.flush()
193	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
194	        except OSError as exc:
195	            return f"cannot write output {target!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}"
196	        try:

198	        except OSError as exc:

200	        tmp_name = None

202	        if tmp_name is not None:

420	# Probabilities are reported in full; entries this close to 0 are omitted
421	# and entries this close to 1 are reported as exactly 1. Reported values

423	_PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE = 1e-15

427	def _snap_probability(value: float) -> float | None:
428	    """Snap one probability for deterministic output.
429	
430	    Returns ``None`` when the entry is omitted (magnitude at most
431	    ``1e-15``), ``1.0`` when it is within ``1e-15`` of 1, and otherwise a
432	    finite ``float`` clamped to ``(0, 1)`` so simulation round-off can
433	    never produce an out-of-range value.
434	    """
435	    if abs(value) <= _PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE:
436	        return None
437	    if abs(1.0 - value) <= _PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE:
438	        return 1.0
439	    return min(1.0, max(0.0, float(value)))

450	    first, mirroring the normalization the sampling path applies to basis
451	    probabilities, so simulation round-off (notably density-matrix drift)
452	    cannot move the reported sum away from 1.
453	    """
454	    aggregated = measurement_probabilities(program, basis_probabilities)
455	    total = math.fsum(aggregated.values())
456	    probabilities: dict[str, float] = {}
457	    for key, value in aggregated.items():
458	        normalized = value / total if total else value
459	        snapped = _snap_probability(normalized)
460	        if snapped is not None:
461	            probabilities[key] = snapped

463	    if noise_model is None:
464	        return {
465	            "schema_version": 1,
466	            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
467	            "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
468	            "probabilities": probabilities,

473	        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
474	        "noise_model": noise_model,

559	            f"batch manifest schema_version must be {BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION}, got {schema_version!r}"
560	        )
561	
562	    if "jobs" not in data:
563	        raise _BatchManifestError("batch manifest is missing required key 'jobs'")
564	    jobs = data["jobs"]
565	    if not isinstance(jobs, list):
566	        raise _BatchManifestError("batch manifest 'jobs' must be an array")
567	    if not 1 <= len(jobs) <= MAX_BATCH_JOBS:
568	        raise _BatchManifestError(
569	            f"batch manifest 'jobs' must contain between 1 and {MAX_BATCH_JOBS} jobs, got {len(jobs)}"
570	        )
571	
572	    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
573	    for index, job in enumerate(jobs):
574	        where = f"job at jobs[{index}]"
575	        if not isinstance(job, dict):
576	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
577	        for key in job:
578	            if key not in _BATCH_JOB_KEYS:
579	                raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} has unknown key {key!r}")
580	
581	        if "id" not in job:
582	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} is missing required key 'id'")
583	        job_id = job["id"]
584	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
585	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'id' must be a non-empty string")
586	        if job_id in seen_ids:
587	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"duplicate job id {job_id!r}")
588	        seen_ids.add(job_id)
589	
590	        if "source" not in job:
591	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} is missing required key 'source'")
592	        source = job["source"]
593	        if not isinstance(source, str):
594	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'source' must be a string")
595	        if source == "-":
596	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'source' must not be '-'; stdin is reserved for the manifest")
597	
598	        if "shots" in job:
599	            shots = job["shots"]
600	            if not _is_json_int(shots) or shots <= 0:
601	                raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'shots' must be a positive integer")
602	
603	        if "seed" in job and not _is_json_int(job["seed"]):
604	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'seed' must be an integer")
605	
606	        if "noise_model" in job:
607	            noise_model = job["noise_model"]
608	            if not isinstance(noise_model, str):
609	                raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'noise_model' must be a string path")
610	            if noise_model == "-":
611	                raise _BatchManifestError(
612	                    f"{where} 'noise_model' must not be '-'; stdin is reserved for the manifest"
613	                )
614	
615	    return jobs

618	def _batch_simulate(manifest_arg: str, ctx: _RunContext | None = None) -> int:
619	    try:
620	        if manifest_arg == "-":
621	            raw_manifest = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
622	            base_dir = os.getcwd()
623	        else:
624	            with open(manifest_arg, "rb") as handle:
625	                raw_manifest = handle.read()
626	            base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(manifest_arg))
627	    except OSError as exc:
628	        _emit_error("io_error", f"cannot read manifest {manifest_arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}")
629	        return 1
630	    if ctx is not None and manifest_arg != "-":
631	        ctx.register_input(manifest_arg)
632	
633	    try:
634	        manifest_text = raw_manifest.decode("utf-8")
635	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
636	        _emit_error("io_error", f"manifest {manifest_arg!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}")
637	        return 1
638	
639	    try:
640	        data = json.loads(
641	            manifest_text,
642	            object_pairs_hook=_manifest_pairs,
643	            parse_constant=_reject_manifest_constant,
644	        )
645	        jobs = _validate_batch_manifest(data)
646	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, _BatchManifestError) as exc:
647	        # Syntax problems are reported with the same shape as every other
648	        # manifest rejection: a single batch_input_error line.
649	        if isinstance(exc, json.JSONDecodeError):
650	            message = f"batch manifest is not valid JSON: {exc}"
651	        else:
652	            message = str(exc)
653	        _emit_error("batch_input_error", message)
654	        return 2
655	
656	    # Register every path the validated manifest names, then guard against
657	    # an input-overwriting export before any task file is opened or any
658	    # simulation runs. References are registered from the manifest itself,
659	    # so a missing/unreadable task is still covered.
660	    if ctx is not None:
661	        _register_manifest_references(ctx, jobs, base_dir)
662	        if (code := _guard_output_conflict(ctx)) is not None:
663	            return code
664	
665	    # Read, decode, parse and validate every task first (task failures are
666	    # embedded), then evolve each prepared circuit in manifest order.
667	    prepared: list[
668	        tuple[dict[str, object], Program | None, dict[str, float] | None, dict[str, object] | None]
669	    ] = []
670	    for job in jobs:
671	        program, noise_model, error, _exit_code = _prepare_simulation(
672	            job["source"],
673	            job.get("noise_model"),
674	            base_dir,
675	            ctx,
676	        )
677	        prepared.append((job, program, noise_model, error))
678	
679	    results: list[dict[str, object]] = []
680	    succeeded = 0
681	    for job, program, noise_model, error in prepared:
682	        output: dict[str, object] | None = None
683	        if error is None:
684	            assert program is not None
685	            output, error, _exit_code = _compute_simulation(
686	                program,
687	                noise_model,
688	                job.get("shots", 1024),
689	                job.get("seed", 0),
690	            )
691	        if error is None:
692	            succeeded += 1
693	            results.append({"id": job["id"], "status": "succeeded", "output": output})
694	        else:
695	            results.append({"id": job["id"], "status": "failed", "error": error})
696	
697	    summary: dict[str, object] = {
698	        "schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION,
699	        "job_count": len(jobs),
700	        "succeeded": succeeded,
701	        "failed": len(jobs) - succeeded,
702	        "results": results,
703	    }
704	    return _finish(ctx, summary, 0 if succeeded == len(jobs) else 3)

745	    result: dict[str, object] = {}

753	def _require_int(value: object, description: str) -> int:
754	    if not _is_json_int(value):

759	def _check_finite_numbers(value: object, description: str) -> None:
760	    """Reject non-finite floats anywhere in an already-parsed JSON payload.
761	
762	    Integers, strings, booleans and ``None`` are unproblematic; floats are
763	    only reachable through explicit decimal literals (constants such as
764	    ``NaN`` are refused at parse time) but must still be finite.
765	    """
766	    if isinstance(value, float):
767	        if not math.isfinite(value):
768	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{description} is not a finite number")
769	    elif isinstance(value, dict):
770	        for key, item in value.items():
771	            _check_finite_numbers(item, f"{description}.{key}")
772	    elif isinstance(value, list):
773	        for index, item in enumerate(value):
774	            _check_finite_numbers(item, f"{description}[{index}]")

777	def _validate_baseline_output(output: object, where: str) -> dict[str, object]:
778	    if not isinstance(output, dict):
779	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
780	    for key in output:
781	        if key not in _OUTPUT_V2_KEYS:
782	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unknown key {key!r}")
783	
784	    for required in _OUTPUT_V1_KEYS:
785	        if required not in output:
786	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key {required!r}")
787	
788	    schema_version = _require_int(output["schema_version"], f"{where} 'schema_version'")
789	    shots = _require_int(output["shots"], f"{where} 'shots'")
790	    seed = _require_int(output["seed"], f"{where} 'seed'")
791	    num_qubits = _require_int(output["num_qubits"], f"{where} 'num_qubits'")
792	    num_clbits = _require_int(output["num_clbits"], f"{where} 'num_clbits'")
793	
794	    if schema_version not in (1, 2):
795	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'schema_version' must be 1 or 2")
796	    if shots <= 0:
797	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'shots' must be a positive integer")
798	    if not 1 <= num_qubits <= 20:
799	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'num_qubits' must be between 1 and 20")
800	    if not 1 <= num_clbits <= 20:
801	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'num_clbits' must be between 1 and 20")
802	
803	    counts = output["counts"]
804	    if not isinstance(counts, dict) or not counts:
805	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' must be a non-empty JSON object")
806	    total = 0
807	    for key, value in counts.items():
808	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
809	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' keys must be non-empty strings")
810	        if not _is_json_int(value) or value <= 0:
811	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' values must be positive integers")
812	        if len(key) != num_clbits or any(bit not in "01" for bit in key):
813	            raise _ReconcileInputError(
814	                f"{where} 'counts' key {key!r} is not a {num_clbits}-bit measurement string"
815	            )
816	        total += value
817	    if total != shots:
818	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' must sum to shots ({shots}), got {total}")
819	
820	    if schema_version == 2:
821	        if num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
822	            raise _ReconcileInputError(
823	                f"{where} noisy output must have at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits"
824	            )
825	        if "noise_model" not in output:
826	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key 'noise_model'")
827	        noise_model = output["noise_model"]
828	        if not isinstance(noise_model, dict) or not noise_model:
829	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'noise_model' must be a non-empty JSON object")
830	        for channel, probability in noise_model.items():
831	            if channel not in _NOISE_CHANNELS:
832	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unknown noise channel {channel!r}")
833	            if isinstance(probability, bool) or not isinstance(probability, (int, float)):
834	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} noise channel {channel!r} must be a number")
835	            if not math.isfinite(float(probability)) or not 0.0 <= float(probability) <= 1.0:
836	                raise _ReconcileInputError(
837	                    f"{where} noise channel {channel!r} probability must be between 0 and 1"
838	                )
839	    elif "noise_model" in output:
840	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} schema_version 1 output must not contain 'noise_model'")
841	
842	    return output

845	def _validate_baseline_error(error: object, where: str) -> dict[str, object]:
846	    if not isinstance(error, dict):
847	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
848	    for key in error:
849	        if key not in _ERROR_KEYS:
850	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unknown key {key!r}")
851	
852	    name = error.get("error")
853	    if not isinstance(name, str) or name not in _RECONCILE_ERROR_NAMES:
854	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'error' must name a batch-simulate task error")
855	    if "message" not in error or not isinstance(error["message"], str):
856	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing a string 'message'")
857	
858	    if name in _POSITIONED_ERROR_NAMES:
859	        for position in ("line", "column"):
860	            if position not in error:
861	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key {position!r}")
862	            value = error[position]
863	            if not _is_json_int(value) or value < 1:
864	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} {position!r} must be a positive integer")
865	    elif "line" in error or "column" in error:
866	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} {name!r} errors must not carry a source position")
867	
868	    return error

871	def _validate_baseline(data: object, jobs: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
872	    """Validate the batch-result *data* against the manifest *jobs*.
873	
874	    Self-consistency and correspondence (count, ids, order) are checked
875	    here, before any task is re-run. Raises :class:`_ReconcileInputError`.
876	    """
877	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
878	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline must be a JSON object")
879	    for key in data:
880	        if key not in _BASELINE_ROOT_KEYS:
881	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"unknown baseline key {key!r}")
882	    if any(key not in data for key in _BASELINE_ROOT_KEYS):
883	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline is missing one or more required root keys")
884	
885	    schema_version = _require_int(data["schema_version"], "baseline 'schema_version'")
886	    if schema_version != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
887	        raise _ReconcileInputError(
888	            f"baseline schema_version must be {BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION}, got {schema_version!r}"
889	        )
890	
891	    job_count = _require_int(data["job_count"], "baseline 'job_count'")
892	    succeeded = _require_int(data["succeeded"], "baseline 'succeeded'")
893	    failed = _require_int(data["failed"], "baseline 'failed'")
894	    if job_count < 0 or succeeded < 0 or failed < 0:
895	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline counters must be non-negative")
896	    if succeeded + failed != job_count:
897	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline 'succeeded' + 'failed' must equal 'job_count'")
898	    if job_count != len(jobs):
899	        raise _ReconcileInputError(
900	            f"baseline job_count {job_count} does not match manifest job count {len(jobs)}"
901	        )
902	
903	    results = data["results"]
904	    if not isinstance(results, list):
905	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline 'results' must be an array")
906	    if len(results) != job_count:
907	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline 'results' length must equal 'job_count'")
908	
909	    seen: set[str] = set()
910	    actual_succeeded = 0
911	    for index, entry in enumerate(results):
912	        where = f"baseline result[{index}]"
913	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
914	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
915	        for key in entry:
916	            if key not in _BASELINE_RESULT_KEYS:
917	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unknown key {key!r}")
918	
919	        if "id" not in entry:
920	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key 'id'")
921	        job_id = entry["id"]
922	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
923	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'id' must be a non-empty string")
924	        if job_id in seen:
925	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"duplicate baseline result id {job_id!r}")
926	        seen.add(job_id)
927	        if job_id != jobs[index]["id"]:
928	            raise _ReconcileInputError(
929	                f"{where} id {job_id!r} does not match manifest id {jobs[index]['id']!r}"
930	            )
931	
932	        if "status" not in entry:
933	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key 'status'")
934	        status = entry["status"]
935	        if status == "succeeded":
936	            if "output" not in entry:
937	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} succeeded result is missing 'output'")
938	            if "error" in entry:
939	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} succeeded result must not contain 'error'")
940	            _validate_baseline_output(entry["output"], f"{where} output")
941	            actual_succeeded += 1
942	        elif status == "failed":
943	            if "error" not in entry:
944	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} failed result is missing 'error'")
945	            if "output" in entry:
946	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} failed result must not contain 'output'")
947	            _validate_baseline_error(entry["error"], f"{where} error")
948	        else:
949	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'status' must be 'succeeded' or 'failed'")
950	
951	        required_keys = (
952	            {"id", "status", "output"} if status == "succeeded" else {"id", "status", "error"}
953	        )
954	        if set(entry) != required_keys:
955	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unexpected keys for status {status!r}")
956	
957	    if actual_succeeded != succeeded or len(results) - actual_succeeded != failed:
958	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline counters do not match result statuses")
959	
960	    return results

963	def _read_reconcile_input(
964	    side: str, arg: str, ctx: _RunContext | None = None
965	) -> tuple[bytes, str | None, int | None]:
966	    """Read one reconcile input, returning ``(raw_bytes, base_dir, error_code)``.
967	
968	    *side* is ``"manifest"`` or ``"baseline"`` and is reported on every
969	    failure via the ``input`` field. On failure the code is 1 for an
970	    unreadable file or invalid UTF-8, after emitting an ``io_error``.
971	    """
972	    try:
973	        if arg == "-":
974	            raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
975	            base_dir = os.getcwd()
976	        else:
977	            with open(arg, "rb") as handle:
978	                raw = handle.read()
979	            base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(arg))
980	    except OSError as exc:
981	        _emit_error(
982	            "io_error",
983	            f"cannot read {side} {arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}",
984	            side=side,
985	        )
986	        return b"", None, 1
987	
988	    try:
989	        raw.decode("utf-8")
990	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
991	        _emit_error("io_error", f"{side} {arg!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}", side=side)
992	        return b"", None, 1
993	
994	    if ctx is not None and arg != "-":
995	        ctx.register_input(arg)
996	
997	    return raw, base_dir, None

1000	def _json_equal(expected: object, actual: object) -> bool:
1001	    """Compare parsed JSON ignoring object key order and whitespace.
1002	
1003	    Array order and scalar values (including int-vs-float distinctions and
1004	    numeric precision) are significant.
1005	    """
1006	    if isinstance(expected, dict) and isinstance(actual, dict):
1007	        if set(expected) != set(actual):
1008	            return False
1009	        return all(_json_equal(expected[key], actual[key]) for key in expected)
1010	    if isinstance(expected, list) and isinstance(actual, list):
1011	        return len(expected) == len(actual) and all(
1012	            _json_equal(left, right) for left, right in zip(expected, actual)
1013	        )
1014	    return expected == actual and type(expected) is type(actual)

1017	def _reconcile(manifest_arg: str, baseline_arg: str, ctx: _RunContext | None = None) -> int:
1018	    if manifest_arg == "-" and baseline_arg == "-":
1019	        # Standard input cannot serve both inputs; do not read it.
1020	        _emit_error(
1021	            "reconciliation_error",
1022	            "manifest and baseline cannot both be read from standard input",
1023	        )
1024	        return 2
1025	
1026	    # Read and decode both inputs fully (manifest first, then baseline) and
1027	    # validate both before any task file is touched.
1028	    raw_manifest, base_dir, code = _read_reconcile_input("manifest", manifest_arg, ctx)
1029	    if code is not None:
1030	        return code
1031	    raw_baseline, _base_dir, code = _read_reconcile_input("baseline", baseline_arg, ctx)
1032	    if code is not None:
1033	        return code
1034	
1035	    try:
1036	        manifest_data = json.loads(
1037	            raw_manifest.decode("utf-8"),
1038	            object_pairs_hook=_manifest_pairs,
1039	            parse_constant=_reject_manifest_constant,
1040	        )
1041	        jobs = _validate_batch_manifest(manifest_data)
1042	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, _BatchManifestError) as exc:
1043	        message = (
1044	            f"batch manifest is not valid JSON: {exc}"
1045	            if isinstance(exc, json.JSONDecodeError)
1046	            else str(exc)
1047	        )
1048	        _emit_error("reconcile_input_error", message)
1049	        return 2
1050	
1051	    try:
1052	        baseline_data = json.loads(
1053	            raw_baseline.decode("utf-8"),
1054	            object_pairs_hook=lambda pairs: _pairs_no_dupes(pairs, "baseline"),
1055	            parse_constant=_reject_baseline_constant,
1056	        )
1057	        _check_finite_numbers(baseline_data, "baseline")
1058	        baseline_results = _validate_baseline(baseline_data, jobs)
1059	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, _ReconcileInputError) as exc:
1060	        message = (
1061	            f"baseline is not valid JSON: {exc}"
1062	            if isinstance(exc, json.JSONDecodeError)
1063	            else str(exc)
1064	        )
1065	        _emit_error("reconcile_input_error", message)
1066	        return 2
1067	
1068	    # Register every path the validated manifest names (plus the manifest
1069	    # and baseline already read), then guard against an input-overwriting
1070	    # export before any task file is opened or any task is re-run.

55	    tbit = 1 << target
56	    step = tbit << 1
57	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
58	        for low in range(base, base + tbit):
59	            if not (low & cbit):
60	                continue
61	            high = low | tbit
62	            a = state[low]
63	            b = state[high]
64	            state[low] = g00 * a + g01 * b
65	            state[high] = g10 * a + g11 * b
66	
67	
68	def _rotation_matrix(kind: str, theta: float) -> tuple[complex, complex, complex, complex]:
69	    """The single-qubit matrix of an rx/ry/rz rotation by *theta* radians."""
70	    c = math.cos(theta / 2)
71	    s = math.sin(theta / 2)
72	    if kind == "rx":
73	        return (c, -1j * s, -1j * s, c)
74	    if kind == "ry":
75	        return (c, -s, s, c)
76	    # rz
77	    return (cmath.exp(-0.5j * theta), 0j, 0j, cmath.exp(0.5j * theta))
78	
79	
80	def _rx(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int, theta: float) -> None:
81	    c = math.cos(theta / 2)
82	    s = math.sin(theta / 2)
83	    bit = 1 << qubit
84	    step = bit << 1
85	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
86	        for low in range(base, base + bit):
87	            high = low | bit
88	            a = state[low]
89	            b = state[high]
90	            state[low] = c * a - 1j * s * b
91	            state[high] = -1j * s * a + c * b
92	
93	
94	def _ry(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int, theta: float) -> None:
95	    c = math.cos(theta / 2)
96	    s = math.sin(theta / 2)
97	    bit = 1 << qubit
98	    step = bit << 1
99	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
100	        for low in range(base, base + bit):
101	            high = low | bit
102	            a = state[low]
103	            b = state[high]
104	            state[low] = c * a - s * b
105	            state[high] = s * a + c * b
106	
107	
108	def _rz(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int, theta: float) -> None:
109	    lo_factor = cmath.exp(-0.5j * theta)
110	    hi_factor = cmath.exp(0.5j * theta)
111	    bit = 1 << qubit
112	    for index in range(1 << num_qubits):
113	        if index & bit:
114	            state[index] = hi_factor * state[index]
115	        else:
116	            state[index] = lo_factor * state[index]
117	
118	
119	def _apply_gate(state: list[complex], op: Operation, num_qubits: int) -> None:
120	    """Apply one (non-measurement) *op* to *state* in place."""
121	    if op.kind == "x":
122	        _pauli_x(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits)
123	    elif op.kind == "h":
124	        _hadamard(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits)
125	    elif op.kind == "cx":
126	        _controlled_x(state, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], num_qubits)
127	    elif op.kind == "cz":
128	        _controlled_single(
129	            state, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], num_qubits, (1 + 0j, 0j, 0j, -1 + 0j)
130	        )
131	    elif op.kind == "rx":
132	        _rx(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits, op.params[0])
133	    elif op.kind == "ry":
134	        _ry(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits, op.params[0])
135	    elif op.kind == "rz":
136	        _rz(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits, op.params[0])
137	    elif op.kind in ("crx", "cry", "crz"):
138	        matrix = _rotation_matrix(op.kind[1:], op.params[0])
139	        _controlled_single(state, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], num_qubits, matrix)
140	
141	
142	def simulate_state_vector(program: Program) -> list[complex]:
143	    """Return the final state vector after applying all quantum gates.
144	
145	    Basis-state integer ``k`` stores qubit ``i`` in bit ``i`` (q[0] is the
146	    least significant bit). Measurements do not collapse the state: the spec
147	    guarantees every measurement comes after every gate and each qubit is
148	    measured at most once, so non-destructive sampling of the final state is
149	    equivalent.
150	    """
151	    n = program.num_qubits
152	    state = [0j] * (1 << n)
153	    state[0] = 1 + 0j
154	
155	    for op in program.operations:
156	        if op.kind == "measure":
157	            # Measurements affect only the sampled classical outcomes.
158	            continue
159	        _apply_gate(state, op, n)
160	    return state
161	
162	
163	def unitary_matrix(program: Program) -> list[list[complex]]:
164	    """Return the full unitary U induced by the gates (pre-measurement).
165	
166	    The matrix acts on basis vectors with qubit ``i`` in bit ``i`` (q[0] is
167	    the least significant bit), matching :func:`simulate_state_vector`.
168	    Measurement operations are ignored. Columns are evolved independently by
169	    applying each gate in source order, so for a circuit with gates G1..Gk the
170	    result is U = Gk @ ... @ G1.
171	    """
172	    n = program.num_qubits
173	    dim = 1 << n
174	    gate_ops = [op for op in program.operations if op.kind != "measure"]
175	
176	    columns: list[list[complex]] = []
177	    for start in range(dim):
178	        state = [0j] * dim
179	        state[start] = 1 + 0j
180	        for op in gate_ops:
181	            _apply_gate(state, op, n)
182	        columns.append(state)
183	
184	    # Transpose columns-of-U into rows.
185	    return [[columns[col][row] for col in range(dim)] for row in range(dim)]
186	
187	
188	def measurement_probabilities(program: Program, basis_probabilities: list[float]) -> dict[str, float]:
189	    """Aggregate basis-state probabilities into classical-outcome probabilities.
190	
191	    Uses the same qubit-to-clbit mapping as :func:`sample_counts` (each
192	    measured qubit contributes its bit to the classical index; unwritten
193	    clbits stay 0) and the same fixed-width, lexicographically ordered key
194	    convention. With no measurements the only possible outcome is the
195	    all-zero string, carrying total probability 1.
196	    """
197	    width = program.num_clbits
198	    measurements = [(op.targets[0], op.targets[1]) for op in program.operations if op.kind == "measure"]
199	
200	    if not measurements:
201	        return {format(0, f"0{width}b") if width else "": 1.0}
202	
203	    aggregated: dict[int, float] = {}
204	    for basis, probability in enumerate(basis_probabilities):
205	        classical = 0
206	        for qubit, clbit in measurements:
207	            if (basis >> qubit) & 1:
208	                classical |= 1 << clbit
209	        aggregated[classical] = aggregated.get(classical, 0.0) + probability
210	
211	    return {
212	        format(classical, f"0{width}b") if width else "": probability
213	        for classical, probability in sorted(aggregated.items())
214	    }
215	
216	
217	def sample_counts(program: Program, state: list[complex], shots: int, seed: int) -> dict[str, int]:
218	    """Draw *shots* samples from *state* deterministically from *seed*.
219	
220	    Returns a mapping from fixed-width classical bit strings (highest clbit
221	    index first) to occurrence counts. Only observed outcomes are present.
222	    """
223	    probabilities = [abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in state]
224	    return sample_counts_from_probabilities(program, probabilities, shots, seed)
225	
226	
227	def sample_counts_from_probabilities(
228	    program: Program, probabilities: list[float], shots: int, seed: int
229	) -> dict[str, int]:
230	    """Draw *shots* samples from explicit basis-state probabilities.
231	
232	    Used by the density-matrix path, which supplies the diagonal of the
233	    final density matrix; sampling semantics match the state-vector path.
234	    """
235	    measurements = [(op.targets[0], op.targets[1]) for op in program.operations if op.kind == "measure"]
236	
237	    total = sum(probabilities)
238	    cumulative = []
239	    running = 0.0
240	    for probability in probabilities:
241	        running += probability / total
242	        cumulative.append(running)
243	    if cumulative:
244	        cumulative[-1] = 1.0
245	
246	    rng = random.Random(seed)
247	    width = program.num_clbits
248	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
249	    for _ in range(shots):
250	        point = rng.random()
251	        # Binary search for the first cumulative value >= point.
252	        lo, hi = 0, len(cumulative)
253	        while lo < hi:
254	            mid = (lo + hi) // 2
255	            if cumulative[mid] < point:
256	                lo = mid + 1
257	            else:
258	                hi = mid
259	        basis = lo
260	
261	        classical = 0
262	        for qubit, clbit in measurements:
263	            if (basis >> qubit) & 1:
264	                classical |= 1 << clbit
265	        key = format(classical, f"0{width}b") if width else ""
266	        counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
267	
268	    return dict(sorted(counts.items()))
269

1	"""Deterministic canonical simplification for the OpenQASM 2.0 subset.
2	
3	The optimizer rewrites the pre-measurement gate sequence into a canonical
4	form while preserving the circuit's transformation up to a global phase and
5	keeping the measurement layout (qubit-to-clbit mapping) intact:
6	
7	* adjacent ``x``/``x``, ``h``/``h`` pairs and ``cx``/``cz`` pairs with
8	  identical control and target cancel ("adjacent" allows intervening gates
9	  on disjoint qubits);
10	* consecutive same-axis ``rx``/``ry``/``rz`` rotations on one qubit merge
11	  into a single rotation, as do consecutive same-axis ``crx``/``cry``/``crz``
12	  rotations with identical control and target;
13	* rotations whose normalized angle has magnitude at most ``1e-12`` are
14	  deleted;
15	* gates acting on disjoint qubits are moved past each other until the
16	  sequence is sorted by a stable key (minimum qubit, maximum qubit, gate
17	  name and parameter text).
18	
19	Simplification passes repeat until the sequence reaches a fixed point, so
20	inputs that differ only in the ordering of independent gates produce
21	byte-identical output. Single-qubit rotation angles are normalized to
22	``(-pi, pi]`` (rendering a value at either boundary as ``pi`` when it is
23	positive). Controlled rotations are normalized to ``(-2*pi, 2*pi]`` instead:
24	their angle is only ``4*pi``-periodic (a ``2*pi`` shift is *not* a global
25	phase of the controlled unitary), so ``2*pi`` is kept rather than deleted.
26	"""
27	
28	from __future__ import annotations
29	
30	import heapq
31	import math
32	from dataclasses import dataclass
33	
34	from .openqasm import Operation, Program
35	
36	# Rotations this small (after normalization to (-pi, pi]) act as the
37	# identity within floating-point precision and are removed.
38	_ANGLE_EPSILON = 1e-12
39	
40	_ROTATIONS = ("rx", "ry", "rz")
41	_CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS = ("crx", "cry", "crz")
42	
43	
44	@dataclass(frozen=True)
45	class Gate:
46	    """A pre-measurement gate with its canonical (normalized) angle."""
47	
48	    kind: str
49	    qubits: tuple[int, ...]
50	    angle: float | None = None
51	
52	    @property
53	    def qubit_set(self) -> frozenset[int]:
54	        return frozenset(self.qubits)
55	
56	
57	def normalize_angle(angle: float) -> float:
58	    """Reduce *angle* modulo ``2*pi`` into the interval ``(-pi, pi]``.
59	
60	    Angles already inside the interval are returned untouched so ordinary
61	    values (e.g. ``0.7``) are not perturbed by floating-point modulo.
62	    """
63	    if -math.pi < angle <= math.pi:
64	        return angle
65	    reduced = (angle + math.pi) % (2.0 * math.pi) - math.pi
66	    if reduced == -math.pi:
67	        return math.pi
68	    return reduced
69	
70	
71	def normalize_controlled_angle(angle: float) -> float:
72	    """Reduce a controlled-rotation angle modulo ``4*pi`` into ``(-2*pi, 2*pi]``.
73	
74	    A controlled rotation by ``theta + 2*pi`` differs from one by ``theta``
75	    by more than a global phase (the unshifted rotation picks up a sign on
76	    the control-1 block only), so the period is ``4*pi`` and ``2*pi`` itself
77	    is kept. Angles already inside the interval are returned untouched.
78	    """
79	    if -2.0 * math.pi < angle <= 2.0 * math.pi:
80	        return angle
81	    reduced = (angle + 2.0 * math.pi) % (4.0 * math.pi) - 2.0 * math.pi
82	    if reduced == -2.0 * math.pi:
83	        return 2.0 * math.pi
84	    return reduced
85	
86	
87	def _format_angle(angle: float) -> str:
88	    """Render a normalized angle deterministically.
89	
90	    Uses the shortest decimal representation that round-trips to the same
91	    float (at most 17 significant digits), which Python writes as plain
92	    decimal or lowercase scientific notation. Negative zero is written as
93	    ``0``.
94	    """
95	    if angle == 0.0:
96	        return "0"
97	    return repr(angle)
98	
99	
100	def _gate_from_operation(op: Operation) -> Gate:
101	    if op.kind in ("cx", "cz"):
102	        return Gate(op.kind, (op.targets[0], op.targets[1]))
103	    if op.kind in _ROTATIONS:
104	        return Gate(op.kind, (op.targets[0],), normalize_angle(op.params[0]))
105	    if op.kind in _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS:
106	        return Gate(
107	            op.kind,
108	            (op.targets[0], op.targets[1]),
109	            normalize_controlled_angle(op.params[0]),
110	        )
111	    return Gate(op.kind, (op.targets[0],))
112	
113	
114	def _sort_key(gate: Gate) -> tuple[int, int, str, str]:
115	    # Ties (including two commuting gates on the same set, e.g. rz/rx) keep
116	    # their relative order, which is the dependency order the semantics need.
117	    parameter = _format_angle(gate.angle) if gate.angle is not None else ""
118	    return (min(gate.qubits), max(gate.qubits), gate.kind, parameter)
119	
120	
121	def _cancels(first: Gate, second: Gate) -> bool:
122	    """True when *second* immediately follows *first* and both vanish."""
123	    if first.qubits != second.qubits:
124	        return False
125	    if first.kind in ("x", "h"):
126	        return first.kind == second.kind
127	    if first.kind in ("cx", "cz"):
128	        return second.kind == first.kind
129	    return False
130	
131	
132	def _merge(first: Gate, second: Gate) -> Gate | None:
133	    """Merge two same-axis rotations on the same qubits, if applicable.
134	
135	    Returns the merged :class:`Gate`, or ``None`` when the gates cannot be
136	    merged. Controlled rotations additionally require identical control and
137	    target and are normalized onto their ``4*pi`` period.
138	    """
139	    if first.kind != second.kind or first.qubits != second.qubits:
140	        return None
141	    if first.kind in _ROTATIONS:
142	        assert first.angle is not None and second.angle is not None
143	        return Gate(first.kind, first.qubits, normalize_angle(first.angle + second.angle))
144	    if first.kind in _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS:
145	        assert first.angle is not None and second.angle is not None
146	        return Gate(
147	            first.kind,
148	            first.qubits,
149	            normalize_controlled_angle(first.angle + second.angle),
150	        )
151	    return None
152	
153	
154	def _is_identity_rotation(gate: Gate) -> bool:
155	    return (
156	        gate.kind in _ROTATIONS + _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS
157	        and gate.angle is not None
158	        and abs(gate.angle) <= _ANGLE_EPSILON
159	    )
160	
161	
162	def _simplify_once(gates: list[Gate]) -> list[Gate] | None:
163	    """Run one simplification sweep.
164	
165	    Scans left to right; whenever a gate can cancel or merge with the
166	    nearest preceding gate that shares a qubit (gates between them acting on
167	    disjoint qubits are ignored), the rewrite is performed and the scan
168	    restarts so the newly adjacent gates become visible. Identity rotations
169	    are dropped on sight. Returns the rewritten list, or ``None`` when no
170	    rewrite was possible.
171	    """
172	    for index in range(len(gates)):
173	        gate = gates[index]
174	        if _is_identity_rotation(gate):
175	            return gates[:index] + gates[index + 1 :]
176	
177	        for earlier in range(index - 1, -1, -1):
178	            previous = gates[earlier]
179	            if previous.qubit_set & gate.qubit_set:
180	                if _cancels(previous, gate):
181	                    return gates[:earlier] + gates[earlier + 1 : index] + gates[index + 1 :]
182	                merged = _merge(previous, gate)
183	                if merged is not None:
184	                    return gates[:earlier] + [merged] + gates[earlier + 1 : index] + gates[index + 1 :]
185	                break
186	    return None
187	
188	
189	def _canonical_order(gates: list[Gate]) -> list[Gate]:
190	    """Return *gates* in canonical order.
191	
192	    Builds the dependency DAG in which each gate depends on the latest
193	    preceding gate touching any of the same qubits (so gates on disjoint
194	    qubits are mutually independent), then takes the unique linear
195	    extension that minimizes :func:`_sort_key` among all available gates at
196	    each step. That extension is independent of how independent gates were
197	    written, which is what makes reordering canonical.
198	    """
199	    count = len(gates)
200	    # predecessors[i]: gates that must precede gate i (share a qubit and come
201	    # earlier in the source). Only the latest such gate per qubit is needed:
202	    # transitively it already requires everything before it.
203	    predecessors: list[set[int]] = [set() for _ in range(count)]
204	    last_on_qubit: dict[int, int] = {}
205	    for index, gate in enumerate(gates):
206	        for qubit in gate.qubits:
207	            if qubit in last_on_qubit:
208	                predecessors[index].add(last_on_qubit[qubit])
209	            last_on_qubit[qubit] = index
210	
211	    remaining = [len(preds) for preds in predecessors]
212	    dependents: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in range(count)]
213	    for index, preds in enumerate(predecessors):
214	        for pred in preds:
215	            dependents[pred].append(index)
216	
217	    # Heap entries break key ties by original position, preserving the
218	    # relative (dependency) order of gates that the sort key cannot separate.
219	    ready: list[tuple[tuple, int]] = [
220	        (_sort_key(gates[index]), index) for index in range(count) if remaining[index] == 0
221	    ]
222	    heapq.heapify(ready)
223	
224	    ordered: list[Gate] = []
225	    while ready:
226	        _, index = heapq.heappop(ready)
227	        ordered.append(gates[index])
228	        for dependent in dependents[index]:
229	            remaining[dependent] -= 1
230	            if remaining[dependent] == 0:
231	                heapq.heappush(ready, (_sort_key(gates[dependent]), dependent))
232	    return ordered
233	
234	
235	def canonical_gates(operations: tuple[Operation, ...]) -> tuple[tuple[Gate, ...], bool]:
236	    """Return ``(gates, changed)``: the canonical gate sequence and whether
237	    any cancellation, merge, deletion or reordering was applied to the
238	    extracted gates.
239	
240	    Angle normalization alone (the same gates in the same order) does not
241	    count as a change.
242	    """
243	    gates = [_gate_from_operation(op) for op in operations if op.kind != "measure"]
244	    changed = False
245	    while True:
246	        simplified = _simplify_once(gates)
247	        if simplified is not None:
248	            gates = simplified
249	            changed = True
250	            continue
251	        ordered = _canonical_order(gates)
252	        if ordered != gates:
253	            gates = ordered
254	            changed = True
255	            continue
256	        return tuple(gates), changed
257	
258	
259	def _gate_line(gate: Gate) -> str:
260	    if gate.kind in ("cx", "cz"):
261	        return f"{gate.kind} q[{gate.qubits[0]}],q[{gate.qubits[1]}];"
262	    if gate.kind in _ROTATIONS:
263	        assert gate.angle is not None
264	        return f"{gate.kind}({_format_angle(gate.angle)}) q[{gate.qubits[0]}];"
265	    if gate.kind in _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS:
266	        assert gate.angle is not None
267	        return (
268	            f"{gate.kind}({_format_angle(gate.angle)}) "
269	            f"q[{gate.qubits[0]}],q[{gate.qubits[1]}];"
270	        )
271	    return f"{gate.kind} q[{gate.qubits[0]}];"
272	
273	
274	def render(program: Program, gates: tuple[Gate, ...]) -> str:
275	    """Render the canonical circuit as complete, re-parseable OpenQASM."""
276	    lines = [
277	        "OPENQASM 2.0;",
278	        'include "qelib1.inc";',
279	        f"qreg q[{program.num_qubits}];",
280	        f"creg c[{program.num_clbits}];",
281	    ]
282	    lines.extend(_gate_line(gate) for gate in gates)
283	    # Measurements sorted by (clbit, qubit), preserving the qubit-to-clbit
284	    # mapping from the source program.
285	    measurements = sorted(
286	        (op.targets[1], op.targets[0])
287	        for op in program.operations
288	        if op.kind == "measure"
289	    )
290	    lines.extend(f"measure q[{qubit}] -> c[{clbit}];" for clbit, qubit in measurements)
291	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
292	
293	
294	def optimize(program: Program) -> tuple[tuple[Gate, ...], bool, str]:
295	    """Return ``(canonical_gates, changed, canonical_qasm)`` for *program*.
296	
297	    *changed* is true only when the pre-measurement gate sequence changed
298	    (cancellation, merge, deletion or reordering); re-rendering the same
299	    gates with normalized angles does not set it.
300	    """
301	    gates, changed = canonical_gates(program.operations)
302	    return gates, changed, render(program, gates)
303

3	本项目是「量子线路仿真与验证平台」的代码仓库，用于逐步实现该方向的线路构建、状态仿真与结果验证能力。
4	
5	当前支持一个 OpenQASM 2.0 子集的状态向量仿真入口 `simulate`、输出末态精确测量概率（不采样）的 `probabilities` 入口、按清单批量执行独立仿真的 `batch-simulate` 入口、按清单重跑并与历史批量结果对账的 `reconcile` 入口、比较两份线路是否等价的 `equivalent` 入口、把线路化简为确定规范结果的 `optimize` 入口、比较两份线路末态并量化单量子位纠缠的 `state-metrics` 入口，以及只解析分析、静态预估线路规模与可执行性的 `estimate` 入口。
6
